# ADR-0003: Docs environments are generated by Trestle and joined to the model

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted |
| Date | 2026-10-17 |
| Supersedes | — |
| Superseded by | — |

## Context

The docs environments under `envs/` (`envs/unitycatalog` in three variants,
plus `envs/aws-sim`) were hand-written Compose. `envs/environments.yml` repeats
facts a planner computes (ports, client env), and the estate model's deployment
layer knows nothing about them. Its one environment, `trustedCompute`, is a
narrative reference deployment.

Trestle's `stack-topology` already plans environments from an `env.toml`
selection and renders Compose, Envoy, client env, and a graph. Its modules
(`unity-catalog`, `rustfs`, `postgres`, …) resemble our implementations and its
roles (`data_catalog`, `object_store`, `tracing`, …) resemble our capabilities,
but neither side knows the other's IDs, so Trestle's graph can't link a node to a
concept, a spec, or a page.

Two forces pull in opposite directions. A module's implementation identity is a
stable 1:1 fact that should travel with the module, including into custom
catalogs. A role's contribution to a capability ("`tracing` is a *partial*
contribution to observability") is an interpretation of our concepts that
Trestle shouldn't carry. The bare Vercel build and the reader bundle also have no
cargo, so nothing in emission can call Trestle.

The design as built is
[`trestle-integration.md`](../design/trestle-integration.md).

## Considered Options

- **Keep hand-written environments; map them to the model by hand.** No new
  tooling, but every port and endpoint stays maintained in three places, and the
  model mapping drifts the same way.
- **All mappings in docs-factory.** Simple ownership, but modules in custom
  Trestle catalogs stay unmapped, and Trestle's own graph still can't say what a
  node is.
- **All mappings in Trestle.** Its graph becomes self-describing, but loses the
  full/partial scope of role contributions, and Trestle ends up carrying our
  semantics.
- **Hybrid ownership, generated and committed environments (chosen).**

## Decision

**Ownership is split by fact type.** A Trestle module carries an optional
`model:` ref naming the implementation it packages (`unity-catalog` →
`unityCatalogOSS`). A role's contribution to a capability or concern, with its
`full`/`partial` scope, lives in docs-factory
(`architecture/integrations/trestle.yaml`). Roles and modules with no mapping are
reported, never filled with an invented capability.

**Environments are generated and committed.** Each docs environment commits its
`env.toml` recipe, its build context, the rendered Compose / Envoy / client env,
and `plan.json` together, against a Trestle revision pinned in
`envs/trestle.toml`. A path-filtered (and nightly) CI job re-renders with the pin
and fails on any diff. Everything downstream reads the committed files, so
emission needs neither Trestle nor Rust.

**`plan.json` is the export contract.** `trestle env render` writes it from the
same settled plan that produces the files. It is Trestle's plan result minus file
bodies, in a versioned envelope with a JSON schema: graph nodes with their
`model:` refs, the service inventory, typed edges with stable composite keys,
surfaces and host/container client contracts, and provenance (schema version,
Trestle revision, recipe digest). It records planned configuration. Health and
test results are separate evidence, and it never carries credentials.

**The join runs in docsnip.** `docsnip envs --fix` reads `plan.json`, the model
export, and the role map, then writes a deployment fragment per environment
(`architecture/model/deployment/generated/<env>.likec4`, tagged `#generated`,
each node `instanceOf` its implementation) and the derived `environments.yml`
facts. `docsnip check` fails on a stale fragment or a dangling reference. Python
is authoritative; JS consumes the emitted JSON and never re-resolves.

**Generated environments and `trustedCompute` stay separate.** A generated
environment is a fact about a docs environment. `trustedCompute` stays
hand-written as the narrative reference deployment. Matching may show which
parts of the reference a generated environment contains, but it never adds
hypothetical services to a generated one. Estate views exclude `#generated`.

## Consequences

### Positive
- Ports, endpoints, and client env have one source, the plan; prose, registry,
  and harness read it instead of repeating it.
- Trestle's graph and the docs site resolve the same node to the same concept.
- Model deployment edges for docs environments trace to plan edges, so they
  can't drift from what CI runs.

### Negative / Trade-offs
- The docs depend on a pinned Trestle revision, and the re-render job pays a
  cold `cargo install` (about 3–5 minutes) when it runs.
- Rendered files are committed. Reviews see generated diffs, and a hand edit to
  a render fails CI.
- Docs-specific needs (the local image, the container name, shared mounts,
  embedded metadata, client-env aliases) become Trestle knobs, so a docs change
  can wait on a Trestle merge and a re-pin.
- Two deployment stories coexist in the model. The `#generated` tag and this ADR
  keep them apart.
